column1: # Rules in omp-port/rules.sed that match no upstream text at the pin, kept on purpose, one per
# line as `left-hand-fragment<TAB>reason`. The fragment is matched as a literal substring of the
# rule's own line, never as a line number, because a line number moves the moment anyone edits a
# rule above it and an exemption that silently stops applying turns the gate red for a reason
# nobody can reconstruct.
# Every entry here has been checked against upstream at the pin named in omp-port/UPSTREAM, and the
# reason says which of the three cases it is:
#   forward-compat net  the left-hand side is a vendor slug family or an exact Cursor phrase that
#                       upstream does not emit today but would have to be translated if it did. The
#                       rule is the only thing standing between that text and a Cursor API in the
#                       tree, so it earns its place by not firing.
#   superseded          upstream reworded the sentence and a different rule now covers the current
#                       phrasing. Kept because the reword is cheap for upstream to undo.
#   orphaned normaliser the rule normalised whitespace in a sentence no rule produces any more. It
#                       can never do harm and cannot do good either; delete it when its subject
#                       comes back.
# Anything stale and not listed here fails `rule staleness`. That is the point: a rule upstream has
# outrun should cost a deliberate decision, not a silent no-op, and the way to make that decision
# cheap is to see the list at every sync instead of finding the residue in a generated skill six
# weeks later.
# Re-checked at: 12d587df (pin). Every rule below was applied in isolation to the raw upstream
# extract and confirmed to change nothing, and was also confirmed to produce no marker in a full
# marked build, which is the intersection that distinguishes stale from merely shadowed.
# forward-compat net. The tier table in section 2 maps every vendor slug family to a capability, so
# that no slug can reach the tree untranslated. `claude-fable-*` and `cursor-grok-*-fast` are the two
# rows upstream does not exercise at this pin, having moved to `claude-opus-*` and bare `grok-*`.
# Dropping a row silently removes a tier, and `untiered slugs` would only notice once upstream
# actually used the slug, at which point the text is already in the tree.
`claude-fable-[0-9.-]+(-(thinking-)?[a-z]+)?`
column2: forward-compat net: judgment tier for a slug family upstream no longer emits at the pin

column1: `cursor-grok-[0-9.]+-([a-z]+-)?fast`
column2: forward-compat net: fast-code tier for Cursor's provider-prefixed grok form, unused at the pin
